mechanisms.price_constraints: A binding daily upper price bound may postpone price discovery, while touching a lower bound and recovering by the close may distinguish temporary selling pressure from continuing weakness. These are competing hypotheses, not observed order-book demand. Actual session bounds, not a hardcoded10percent rule, identify events.
mechanisms.session_conflict: A close-to-close change can result from overnight repricing or active-session movement. Opposing overnight/intraday directions may distinguish acceptance from rejection of the opening price. Aggregated1/5/20day returns used before do not retain this decomposition.

upper-close.selected: raw close within half tick of upper bound
upper-close.expected_difference: selected minus control >0 for continued net return

lower-recovery.selected: raw low touches lower bound within half tick and close is more than half tick above it
lower-recovery.control: ret1<=mature-training q10 and no lower-bound touch

gap-down-repair.selected: adjusted open<previous adjusted close and close>open
gap-down-repair.control: same negative opening gap and close<=open

gap-up-fade.control: same positive opening gap and close>=open
gap-up-fade.expected_difference: control minus selected >0; avoidance information, not a short-sale strategy
